descriptions.root: The single-asset runtime as its own repository. Working path: AGENTS.md → module names → README_module_<name>.md → the module's own skills → code.
descriptions.Makefile: Entrypoint of everything — per-asset fan-out, JOBS measured from cores and memory, the host port from the ports in use, OMP threads pinned to 1 for determinism.
descriptions.docker-compose.yml: One image, two anchors: what every service is, and the one command the dashboard and the assets add.
descriptions.module_data/: Ingest — venue downloads, Lean ZIPs, one canonical DuckDB per asset.
descriptions.module_data/ingest.py: Selects one venue's whole candle per minute into the asset's canonical series (primary-failover, full grid).
descriptions.module_data/lean.py: The Lean-exact raw format — the one external-format boundary; the raw tree is written so a Lean backtest could read it directly.
descriptions.module_data/skills/: The module's own contract: candle canonicalisation, and the acquisition methodology beside it.
descriptions.module_ml/: Research — bars, features, triple-barrier labels, purged walk-forward XGBoost.
descriptions.module_ml/skills/: The module's own contract: the research methodology, equation by equation.
descriptions.module_ml/validation.py: Purged walk-forward splits and the frozen final holdout — the gate of the whole system.
descriptions.module_monitoring/: Presentation of what the runtime modules measured, and the one server that serves it.
descriptions.module_monitoring/serve.py: The one server, two roles: the dashboard, and a container reporting itself.
descriptions.module_monitoring/skills/: The module's own contract: the dashboard conventions, the drawing and the DevOps panel.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_dx/: This drawing: the tracked tree rendered by hand with `make monitoring-dx-update`.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_devops/: The DevOps panel, and the one container that holds the docker socket.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_devops/serv: The Docker Engine over its unix socket: the views, and the three verbs offered for this project's own containers.
descriptions.module_skills/: Repository-wide skills, and the index of the skills each module owns.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/: Per-asset artifacts — one folder per ticker, the asset's whole namespace: its database and every research file beside it. The raw tree and the run records are untracked, so this view does not hold them.

descriptions.root: The same tracked tree, read forward: every file and folder seated beside the primitive it would run on or live in — the column *the same responsibility elsewhere* of the mapping table in `module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md`, its primitives drawn as icons with the flows between them. One host with a durable volume is the home of every store, object storage its copy after the run, the stages the states of one machine. Described and drawn, built nowhere.
descriptions.image_registry: A container image in a registry (Amazon ECR): `mlops-portfolio-1m-pipeline`, the one runtime package every task runs — built from the tree, pulled by the task host; it carries the code only once the ladder of `module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md` § The retrain runtime is a ladder reaches the phase named *the image carries the code*, and until then the volume carries it, as the bind mount does today.
descriptions.Dockerfile: The recipe of the one image, `mlops-portfolio-1m-pipeline`: a dependency layer, built from the tree and pushed to the registry beside it; the code rides the volume until the image carries it — the phase of that name in `module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md` § The retrain runtime is a ladder.
descriptions.requirements.txt: The image's dependency layer, resolved when the image is built and read by no task at run time.
descriptions.task_host: One Linux container instance (Amazon ECS on Amazon EC2): the one host every asset's runs share, its durable volume beside it. It pulls the image, runs the one task definition the state machine starts — once per stage, once per asset — and keeps the dashboard, the panel and one `asset-<ticker>` running as services, one per service, as the residents are kept running here, reached by port-forward and by no public port. `ASSET` is a namespace, never a host of its own; AWS Fargate would be the same task without the host, and so without the volume.
descriptions.store_volume: A durable block volume mounted at `/app` by every task and service of the instance (Amazon EBS): `.:/app` read as `<volume>:/app`, so every `store_*` root and both snapshots sit at the path its `config.py` builds today, the whole-file lock holds, and no stage changes. The home of state, and of the code until the image carries it; the three stores on the island beside it are its copy, taken whole after the last stage of a run has exited, never by a stage and never mid-run.
descriptions.docker-compose.yml: One task definition parameterised by `ASSET`, registered with the service that runs it on the host beside it — never a new unit per asset — and the residents — the dashboard, the panel and one `asset-<ticker>` per ticker — as services kept running, one per service, as they are here; the anchors are its local spelling, one service per ticker written out so the parameter stays visible, and `.:/app` is `<volume>:/app` read forward.
descriptions.log_streams: Log streams keyed by stage and container, and metrics (Amazon CloudWatch): every task's output and the 1 s samples `record.py` keeps in the run record today, shipped off the host. Absent here — described.
descriptions.data_ingest_task: The data-ingest task: the one task definition run with a `module_data` command (`RunTask` with the command overridden, on the task host) — DownloadMarketData and PublishStatus for data once for the basket, BuildCanonicalData once per asset with `ASSET` overridden — that fetches the venues' public endpoints, writes the raw tree and the asset's canonical market object on the volume and exits, holding nothing between runs.
descriptions.module_data/: The code of the data-ingest task: the venue downloads, the Lean raw format, ingest into the canonical market object and the data status — it rides the volume until the image carries it (the phase of that name in `module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md` § The retrain runtime is a ladder), and runs in the task beside it.
descriptions.module_data/config.py: `TICKERS`, the one definition of the basket, and the descriptors that name the raw and canonical objects — `research_ohlcv_duckdb()` and `artifact_dir()`, both here, both resolving unchanged on the volume, the copy's key being each path relative to `STORE_ASSETS_ARTIFACTS_DIR`; `--tickers <TICKER>` — `ASSET` at the container boundary — is the parameter an asset-scoped run takes.
descriptions.module_data/ingest.py: The BuildCanonicalData state: reads the raw tree under a venue and symbol prefix on the volume and writes the canonical market object beside it — the storage → ML-compute line begins at its output.
descriptions.module_data/lean.py: The Lean-exact raw format — the whole of Lean's presence here; the strategy host would read the raw objects in this format directly.
descriptions.module_data/status.py: The PublishStatus state for data: one status object for the whole basket, written by the one-off run and never fanned out; its move to its own prefix, `status/`, would turn five points — the two path constants, the directory `serve.py` serves, the two literal fetches — listed in `module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md` § What stays as it is, and why.
descriptions.module_data/skills/: The module's own contract travels inside the task's code: a document, not a primitive.
descriptions.asset_store: Object storage with one prefix per asset and version (Amazon S3): `artifacts/<ticker>/<version>/`, the version the run's execution name — the asset folder copied whole from the volume after the run: the one database file and the parquets and JSONs beside it. The copy, never the home; the strategy host reads it here.
descriptions.raw_store: Raw objects under a venue and symbol prefix (Amazon S3): `raw/<venue>/<symbol>/<day>`, one object per UTC day, each written once — the raw tree copied from the volume after the run, Lean-exact so the strategy host could read it as it is. Here it is `store_raw_1m/`, on disk and untracked, so the development view does not hold it.
descriptions.run_store: Run and status objects in object storage (Amazon S3): `runs/<run_id>/` — the record `record.py` writes on the volume from inside whichever task ran the stage — and `status/`, the two snapshots' own prefix, both copied from the volume after the run. The reader on the host reads the files on the volume, not this copy. Here it is `store_run_records/`, on disk and untracked, and the snapshots tracked beside the page.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/: The asset folders and their home: one folder per ticker on the volume, the tracked README and parameters two of its files; the store beside it is this folder's copy after the run, never its home.
descriptions.store_assets_artifacts/BTC/: The `BTC` folder on the volume: `BTC_research_ohlcv.duckdb` as the one embedded database — the two venue tables, the canonical table and its three aggregations under one whole-file lock, one writer at a time — copied whole to `artifacts/BTC/<version>/` after the run with the parquets and JSONs keyed `BTC_<artifact>` beside it; never a database process.
descriptions.ml_research_task: The ml-research task: the same task definition run with a `module_ml` command and `ASSET` overridden (`RunTask` with `ASSET=<TICKER>`, on the same host), one run per stage from AggregateBars to EvaluateStrategy inside a Map over the basket as wide as `JOBS`, and PublishStatus for ML once for the basket, never per asset — reading and writing the asset's folder on the volume, and holding nothing between runs.
descriptions.module_ml/: The code of the ml-research task: bars, features, labels, search, model, strategy evaluation and the ML status — it rides the volume until the image carries it (the phase of that name in `module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md` § The retrain runtime is a ladder), and runs in the task beside it, one `ASSET` at a time.
descriptions.module_ml/bars.py: The AggregateBars state, and the one write across the storage → ML-compute line: the three aggregation tables are a pure function of the canonical series, written into the same file on the volume the task read.
descriptions.module_ml/config.py: The descriptors that name every artifact object under the asset prefix, built on `artifact_dir()` of `module_data/config.py` and consumed by descriptor everywhere; the copy's key is each descriptor's path relative to `STORE_ASSETS_ARTIFACTS_DIR`, so a version prefix edits nothing here.
descriptions.module_ml/validation.py: The gate of the whole system, and the same gate wherever it runs: purged walk-forward folds and the frozen final holdout are code inside the task, not a primitive.
descriptions.module_ml/status.py: The PublishStatus state for ML: the basket's status object as a fold over completed asset artifacts, and each asset's README as an artifact object under its prefix; the snapshot's move to its own prefix, `status/`, would turn the same five points as the data snapshot's — the two path constants, the directory `serve.py` serves, the two literal fetches (`module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md` § What stays as it is, and why).
descriptions.module_ml/skills/: The research methodology travels inside the task's code: a document, not a primitive.
descriptions.dashboard_front: A static front (Amazon S3 with Amazon CloudFront): the page files and the two snapshots served with no process rendering them — only when a reader outside the host appears; until then the reader container beside it serves them from the volume. Absent here — described.
descriptions.reader_container: The `dashboard` service kept running on the task host: the `/containers`, `/runs` and `/devops/*` routes of `serve.py`, reading the run records and the snapshots on the volume and reaching the asset services and the panel by name as here; reached from outside by port-forward, where `ssh -L` stands today, and by no public port.
descriptions.module_monitoring/: The page files — the page, its scripts, the two snapshots — served by the reader container beside them from the volume, the static front absent; `serve.py`'s routes are that container's code, and `record.py` the tasks'.
descriptions.module_monitoring/config.py: Every address the reader knows — the internal port, the service names, the run record's paths — built once here; no code depends on a container name.
descriptions.module_monitoring/serve.py: Three things in one file: every file it serves is served by the reader container from the volume, its `/containers`, `/runs` and `/devops/*` routes are that container, and its asset role, `/status`, is the `asset-<ticker>` service beside it — a local mechanism the host keeps, with no primitive of its own.
descriptions.module_monitoring/record.py: Writes the run record on the volume from inside whichever task ran the stage; its logs and 1 s samples are the log streams and metrics on the task host's island.
descriptions.module_monitoring/index.html: The page: a file on the volume, served by the reader container as it is here; no static front serves it.
descriptions.module_monitoring/data_status.json: A status object produced by data compute and read by the page — tracked beside the page today so a fresh clone opens on real numbers; its move to its own prefix, `status/`, would turn five points — the two path constants, the directory `serve.py` serves, the two literal fetches — listed in `module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md` § What stays as it is, and why.
descriptions.module_monitoring/ml_status.json: A status object produced by ML compute, a fold over completed asset artifacts — tracked beside the page today; its move to its own prefix, `status/`, would turn the same five points — the two path constants, the directory `serve.py` serves, the two literal fetches (`module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md` § What stays as it is, and why).
descriptions.module_monitoring/skills/: The page's conventions, this drawing's contract and the panel's travel with the code: documents, not primitives.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_dx/: The repository's view — this drawing, a static object beside the page and served as the page is, and not project code.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_devops/: The engine's views — a console, not project code; the socket it holds is the same socket on the instance, because the service that runs the tasks starts them through the host's own daemon.
descriptions.module_monitoring/sub_module_devops/serv: The one container that holds the docker socket: a console over the engine's own inventory — the same socket on the instance, unchanged.
descriptions.strategy_host: A separate Linux instance running QuantConnect Lean (Amazon EC2): one strategy container — a lean-backtest task, or one that stays running and trades live — reading the raw objects in Lean's own format and the research artifacts under the asset prefix, its brokerage credentials read once from the secrets store when it starts. No Lean runtime, container or dependency exists in this repository. Absent here — described.
descriptions.brokerage_secret: A secret in a secrets store (AWS Secrets Manager): the brokerage credentials the strategy host reads when it starts to trade live. Locally there is none — the venue downloads use public endpoints, and neither the dashboard nor the panel asks for a credential. Absent here — described.
descriptions.state_machine: A state machine whose states are the stages (AWS Step Functions): DownloadMarketData → BuildCanonicalData → AggregateBars → GenerateFeatures → GenerateLabels → SearchHyperparameters → TrainModel → EvaluateStrategy → PublishStatus, then PublishStores — the copy of every store to its prefix after the last stage has exited. Every per-asset state is a Map over `TICKERS` — 1 wide for BuildCanonicalData, `JOBS` wide above it; the execution name is `run_id`. It starts each task on the host and sits above every stage and inside none — which is why its flows rise over the picture; the Makefile's `all:` and `ml-all:` are the same order, read locally.
descriptions.event_rule: A schedule and a condition state (Amazon EventBridge Scheduler; a Step Functions choice): the schedule starts the machine once per `download_cadence_minutes`, a fixed offset after midnight UTC so that the day the download asks for is already full — `is_full_utc_day()` in `module_data/lean.py`; the condition asks the volume whether this asset needs its artifacts rebuilt, and gates the states from AggregateBars on. Today the cadence is a hand typing `make docker-all`, and the condition the downloaders' day-presence skip and the rerun table of `methodology_ml.md` § 11, read by a human. Absent here — described.
descriptions.Makefile: The local spelling of the state machine beside it: `all:` and `ml-all:` list the state order, `xargs -P $(JOBS)` is the Map's width, `RUN_ID` the execution name, the fan-out runs one asset's stages in its container, and nothing here schedules — the developer interface, never a scheduler.
descriptions.module_skills/: Repository-wide skills and the name register (`module_skills/glossary.md`): they travel with the code and deploy nowhere — not project code, not a primitive, and the contract of every boundary this picture draws.
descriptions.module_skills/skill_pre_aws_solution.md: The mapping table this view draws: its left column is the other view of this page, its column *the same responsibility elsewhere* is these primitives.
descriptions.AGENTS.md: The contract, where every boundary on this picture was decided; it deploys nowhere and governs everything that does.
descriptions.README.md: The overview: the domain drawing, and § Architectural direction, where this stance is stated in one paragraph.
descriptions.REPORT_pre_aws_minimalism.md: The review of these seats for excess: what could be less, and whether it is; it deploys nowhere and names no primitive the table does not.
